meta.title: How to use | Typle
meta.description: How to start practicing in Typle, create word lists, read your records, where your data is saved, and keyboard shortcuts.

title: How to use
intro: Everything from getting started with practice to creating word lists, reading your records, and where your data is saved. All features work without signing in.

sample.title: Practice with a sample
sample.text: A sample list is included, so you can start right away. Just type the words shown on screen.

create.title: Make your own pack
create.text: Register the words you want to learn as a pack, together with its first list. You can also import them from a CSV or TSV file.

review.title: Review your records
review.text: When you finish a list, your record is saved automatically, so you can check your personal best and how your time changes.

practice.lead: Choose a word list in <play>Practice</play> and type the words shown.

colors.title: Input colors
colors.text: If you type a wrong character, everything from that position on turns red, and the input field shows at which character the mismatch starts. Fix it with <keys>Backspace</keys>. For words whose displayed text differs from what you type (for example, typing “cafe” for “café”), the characters to type appear below the word and are colored instead.

flow.title: How practice works
flow.p1: When every character matches, you move on to the next word. The practice ends after the last word.
flow.p2: Time is measured from your first keystroke until you finish. While you practice, the elapsed time, speed (correct characters per minute), accuracy, and number of mistakes are shown.
flow.p3: Text typed with an IME (such as Japanese) is checked once it is confirmed; characters still being converted are not checked. Pasting and drag-and-drop input are disabled.
flow.p4: The next 3 words appear below the progress bar, and “Show all words” lets you see the whole list.
flow.p5: The eye button at the top shows or hides the live stats (elapsed time, speed, accuracy and mistakes). Your choice is saved in this browser. Hiding them does not change timing or saving, and the result screen still shows the numbers.

choose.title: Choosing a pack, list and device
choose.p1: Click “Pack › List” at the top to choose a pack and switch the list you practice. Packs are ordered by most recent practice and can be searched by pack name, category, tag, list name or word. A pack with one list selects that list right away. In a pack with several lists, lists with a difficulty are chosen with difficulty buttons, and lists without one with name buttons. You can also pick one from the list on the right (below on smartphones).
choose.p2: If you choose another list in the middle of a practice, you are asked to confirm before stopping. An unfinished practice is not recorded.
choose.p3: “Start over” or <keys>Esc</keys> starts the same list over from the beginning.
choose.p4: Use “Device” at the top to choose the device you are practicing on before typing the first character (<devicesSection>Register devices</devicesSection>).

lists.lead: Create a new pack in <create>Create a pack</create>, and edit saved packs and lists in <edit>Word packs</edit>.

packs.title: Packs and lists
packs.p1: Word lists are organized into packs. When you create a pack, you enter the pack’s name and its first list.
packs.p2: Use “Add a list” in a pack’s “…” menu to add a list to a saved pack.
packs.p3: Use “Edit pack” in a pack’s “…” menu to change its name, description, category, and tags, or to reorder the lists inside it.
packs.p4: In the list editor, you can choose which pack the list belongs to (this moves it to another pack). You can also enter one difficulty for the words.

files.title: Copying packs, pack files, and official packs
files.p1: “Duplicate” in a pack’s “…” menu copies the pack with all its lists. The copy is named “Name (copy)” and placed right after the original. Practice history is not copied.
files.p2: “Export” in a pack’s “…” menu saves the pack to a “pack-name.typle-pack.json” file. It contains the name, description, category, tags, lists, and words, but not practice history.
files.p3: Choose that file with “Import from file” to import it as a new pack (this also works when you have no packs yet). Files up to 1 MiB are accepted, and unreadable files are refused. If a pack with the same name exists, the new one is named “Name (2)”.
files.p4: In “Official packs” under Word packs, “Add” puts a ready-made pack into your own packs. You can edit an added pack freely, and packs you already have show “Added”. An official pack you deleted can be added again (its practice history does not come back).

share.title: Sharing a pack
share.p1: When you are logged in, "Share" in a pack's "…" menu creates a share link. Choose "Create link", then "Copy" it and send it to others.
share.p2: Anyone with the link can see the pack's name, description, lists, and words without logging in, and add it to their own packs with "Add to my packs". Your practice records and your name are not visible.
share.p3: Editing the pack does not change the link automatically. "Update share" brings it up to date (the link stays the same). "Stop sharing" ends the link, and it then shows that the share has ended. A shared pack is marked "Shared".
share.p4: Deleting a shared pack also ends its share.

input.title: Entering words
input.p1: Enter a list name and, for each word, the “Word to display” and the “Text to type”. The note is optional.
input.p2: If you leave the characters to type empty, the displayed word is typed as is.
input.p3: Reorder words by dragging, from the “…” menu, or with <keys>Alt+↑↓</keys>. <keys>Enter</keys> moves to the next word, and adds a new row on the last word.

cannotSave.title: When a list cannot be saved
cannotSave.p1: Lists with empty rows, lists without words, and lists with the same name as another list in the same pack cannot be saved.
cannotSave.p2: A list can hold up to 1,000 words, and you can save up to 150 lists.
cannotSave.p3: If you have unsaved changes, you are asked to confirm before canceling or going back in the browser.
cannotSave.p4: If you change the number of words, earlier records drop out of the best-record rankings (the records themselves are kept; see <wordCount>When the word count changes</wordCount>).

manage.title: Managing lists
manage.p1: In <edit>Word packs</edit>, you can search by pack name, list name, or word and change the sort order.
manage.p2: From a pack’s “…” menu you can practice, edit the pack, add a list, or delete it. Deleting a pack also deletes its lists and their practice history. Each list row has its own “…” menu for best records, practice history, CSV export, duplicating, and deleting.
manage.p3: Duplicating copies only the words, not the practice history. The same applies when you duplicate a pack.

csv.title: CSV and TSV files
csv.p1: While editing a list, choose a file with “Import CSV/TSV”. After reviewing its contents, you can add the words to the end of the current ones or replace them.
csv.p2: The first row holds the column names. input (characters to type) and display (word to display) are required; annotation (note) is optional. You can import UTF-8 files of up to 1 MiB and 1,000 words.
csv.p3: “Export CSV” writes each word’s input, display text, and note to a UTF-8 CSV file (practice history is not included). Exported files can be imported as they are.

records.lead: When you finish a practice, the record is saved automatically.

complete.title: Completion screen
complete.p1: Shows the time, accuracy and number of mistyped characters, speed, number of words, and device.
complete.p2: Accuracy is the share of typed characters that were correct. Deletions are not counted, but characters you retype after a correction are.
complete.p3: When you beat your personal best, a badge and the difference from your previous best are shown.
complete.p4: “Again” (<keys>Enter</keys>) lets you practice the same list right away. If saving fails, press “Try saving again”.

history.title: Practice history
history.p1: <records>Practice history</records> lists your practices by date, newest first, and can be filtered by list or device. Filters are kept in the URL, so you can open the same view from a bookmark or link.
history.p2: When filtered by a list, it shows how many times you have practiced that list and your best, and you can start practicing right away with “Practice”. Choosing a pack limits the list choices to that pack’s lists. Records of packs with two or more lists show “pack › list”.
history.p3: The best record of each list is marked “Best”. When you delete a best, the confirmation shows which record will become the next best.

best.title: Best records
best.p1: Choose a list in <rankings>Best records</rankings> to see your personal best, the average of your last 5 runs, how your time has changed, and your top records. The best-records screen groups lists by pack. Each pack shows its practice count, how many lists you have practiced (n/m practiced), when you last practiced, and how many lists set a new best in the last 7 days. Sorting applies to packs, and the lists inside a pack stay in difficulty order.
best.p2: You can switch the ranking between “Accuracy first” (highest accuracy first, then fastest) and “Speed first”, and filter it by device. The selected list and options are kept in the URL.
best.p3: The practice screen also shows the top 5 records for the selected list and highlights your latest one.

wordCount.title: When the word count changes
wordCount.p1: After you add or remove words in a list, only records practiced with the current number of words are ranked. The bests on the practice screen and in practice history follow the same rule.
wordCount.p2: Records with a different word count can be added to the ranking with “Include” in Best records. If there are no records with the current word count yet, records with a different word count are ranked.

home.title: Home
home.text: Once you have at least one record, <home>Home</home> shows this week’s practice count, your practice streak, average accuracy, and practice time, which list to practice next, and how seconds per word and accuracy have changed for each list. Days follow your device’s clock, and weeks start on Monday.

devices.lead: Register the computers and keyboards you practice on in <devices>Devices</devices>, and your records will show which device you used.
devices.p1: The device you choose with “Device” on the practice screen is remembered in this browser and used for your next practice too. Until you choose one, “Default” is used.
devices.p2: You can filter practice history and best records by device.
devices.p3: Renaming a device does not change earlier records; they keep the name the device had when you practiced. You can register up to 100 devices.

storage.lead: Signing in is optional. Where your data is saved depends on whether you are signed in.

browser.title: Saved in this browser
browser.when: When you are not signed in
browser.p2: Data is saved in this browser’s LocalStorage and is not synced with other devices or browsers.

account.title: Saved to your account
account.when: When you sign in with GitHub
account.p1: Data is saved on a server dedicated to your account, so you can use the same data on any device you sign in on.

warning.title: When data is lost
warning.p1: Data saved in this browser is deleted when you clear the browser’s site data. You can back up important lists with “Export CSV”.
warning.p2: Deleting a list also deletes its practice history.

notes.p1: The two storage locations keep their data separately, and nothing is moved automatically when you sign in.
notes.p2: Data from an earlier version (v0.1.x) can be added to the current storage location with the migration button on <home>Home</home>.
notes.p3: If saving fails because changes were made in several windows at once, load the latest data and try again.

shortcuts.lead: Keys you can use instead of the mouse.

screens.editor: Create a list / Edit a word list

actions.resume: Return to typing after clicking outside the input field
actions.next: Move to the next word (adds a row on the last word)
actions.move: Move a word up or down
